Hover (translational): [FAA-H-8083-25B p.4] Effective translational lift (ETL) is the additional lift gained when the helicopter accelerates through approximately 16 to 24 knots. In a hover, the rotor tip-path plane is roughly parallel to the ground and the downwash is recirculated, reducing efficiency.

[UH-1 IPC p.42] During initial hover instruction, emphasize the correlation of cyclic, collective, and pedals. The student must develop a smooth, coordinated input to maintain a stabilized hover within a three-foot tolerance.
Emergency - auto-rotation: [UH-1 IPC p.88] Autorotation entry: lower the collective to the full down position smoothly and promptly to maintain Nr (rotor RPM). Simultaneously apply right pedal to counter torque reduction and establish the proper glide attitude.
Risk Management: [FAA-H-8083-25B p.17] The 5P check (Plan, Plane, Pilot, Passengers, Programming) and the PAVE checklist (Pilot, Aircraft, EnVironment, External pressures) are single-pilot risk-management tools.
